utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D157 will be Exhibit D227.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the judiciary bodies were informed about a crime which happened sometime in November 1991 in Dalj mountains -- in Dalj, as a matter of fact. Apparently a number of Hungarians were killed there on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were never informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would refer to P2093. It should not be broadcasted. And it is at paragraph 76 and -- 76 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do we have a tab?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is tab -- sorry, it is tab --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot find the tab. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, tab -- it is tab 648.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Now, next question is: Can it be shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, not under your guide-lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Anyway, I could -- I could state for -- I could put the question to the witness from this document and it is just for your reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Go ahead. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In January 1992, military bodies conducted an investigation about the crimes which had occurred in Dalj mountains. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me whether I know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You, the government, the judiciary bodies, did you know anything?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any information about that event from military bodies? And when I say "you," I mean you, the government, the judiciary bodies of the Republic of Serbian Krajina? Did you receive any subsequent information about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I expected your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with the Dusan Boljevic case?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just briefly tell us what happened? Who was in charge of the proceedings in that case?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of killings happened in Baranja. It was the military investigation bodies that were in charge of the first phase of the proceedings. The file was in the hands of the military investigating judge in Belgrade until the moment the military withdrew, and then the military judiciary bodies declared themselves incompetent and returned the case to us. We conducted the proceedings at the higher court in Beli Manastir. We convicted Mr. Boljevic to the maximum prison penalty of 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to him after that?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I thought that he was serving his sentence, but then I heard that he had died.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see, please, 1D1034.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is confidential. Sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Should we go into private session or?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It -- I'll not discuss anymore this particular document, and this part might be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we remove it from the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I interrupted you. I apologise for that. You were talking about the military judiciary bodies in the Republic of Serbian Krajina from the moment the republic was set up. Were military courts ever set up?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never in a legal way. For a short period of time, when I was no longer minister of justice, they were indeed set up. But still they couldn't take off the ground. They were never operational. Why? Because the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Police did not adhere to the provisions of the law, according to which the judges of the military courts and military prosecutors had to be appointed by the president. They started doing it themselves, bypassing the authorities of the president of Republic of Serbian Krajina. That's how they compounded the whole situation and made the whole process unlawful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that some illegal military courts, as it were, were set up?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were set up in an unlawful way. Defence counsels appealed against their judgements. And even if those judgements were well-grounded, they had to be overturned on formal and legal grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, do you remember if you had any written correspondence with Mr. Thornberry?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that we exchanged several written documents. I don't know what specifically do you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Thornberry ever address you with regard to the confiscation of Croatian property in the Republic of Serbian Krajina? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did do that. When that letter of his or that inquiry was drafted, it was not based on proper information from his associates. We never applied any measures in respect of the -- a decision. We never confiscated any property. This could be done only by a court, and I informed Mr. Thornberry about that in a letter. I believe that he took it under advisement, and after that he didn't have any inquiries with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he meant by "confiscation"?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to say something about that. When his associates told him that we had a temporary hold of other people's property, they interpreted that as a permanent situation and they erroneously concluded that we were confiscating Croatian property and giving it to somebody else for their use. And that was not correct because on the other hand we received complaints from the Serbs who were in temporary possession of that property. We strictly paid attention to that, and we did not want the status of ownership and the title and deed to ever be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you explain that, either orally or in writing, to Mr. Thornberry and his associates?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I sent my letter directly to Mr. Cedric Thornberry. I explained everything to him and it was accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, did he additionally address you on this issue? Did he ask for additional information?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were minister of justice in the government of the RSK and even in -- earlier in the government of SBWS, did you have any meetings with international representatives where they perhaps complained against certain acts of the judiciary or some specific cases? Did they ever say that the judiciary was not acting properly, failing to prosecute perpetrators of crimes against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never addressed me directly. Whether they talked to the judges in the supreme court, I don't know and the judges didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about certain problems that the judiciary faced during the time they were being established in October 1991. What happened with the courts that, before the beginning of the conflict until July 1991, existed and operated in the territory of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that in this part of the Croatia, there were two courts: The municipal court in Beli Manastir and the district court. And there were prosecutors' offices, municipal and district one. They were both under the district court in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened with these institutions and the personnel, including judges, when the war began? For instance, the court in Beli Manastir and the court in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal court in Beli Manastir and the prosecutor's office in Beli Manastir remained intact. The municipal court in Vukovar and the municipal prosecutor's office in Vukovar fell apart completely. A number of judges were arrested by the Croatian authorities, others were expelled. Later, the courthouse was demolished and we had to rebuild everything from scratch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Indeed, we take the second break. 30 minutes. We'll be back at 12.45. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I'm told that you have 15 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour, and I respectfully ask for 15 minutes more to complete my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 15 minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 15 minutes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- more?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- plus 15 minutes. It is actually 30 minutes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. If we can limit it to that, that's not a big problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I will use one document. It is actually not on our list, Rule 65 ter list, but it is the extract of the document already admitted into evidence. It is P1597, the tab number 572. These are minutes from the Assembly of RSK from 20 of April, 1993, and some parts of this documents have been translated and admitted into evidence and we translated one page for the purpose to show to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you added a one-page translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If there is no objection from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, this is the first I heard about this, Your Honour, so I don't even know what the document is about. And maybe the witness shouldn't either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, it is -- this is the minutes from the Assembly of the RSK held on 20 of April, 1993, and this particular page was actually nomination -- election of the government of Djordje Bjegovic, of the new government, and it indicates when the witness ceased to be a minister of justice in the RSK government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And how come the Prosecution doesn't know about this in advance? It's a question I'd -- for you, Mr. Zivanovic, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution says, "I don't know in advance."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We put it on our list for this witness. It is, as I said, tab 572, and we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- put the translation of the document on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, sorry, it is -- sorry, sorry. It is 1597 from the Prosecution Rule 65 ter list. 1597.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry. I'm at a loss. I don't know what is at issue here. If 1597 is on the Defence's list for this witness, is this a new page that wasn't previously disclosed to the Prosecution? I just don't know. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: As I understand it, Mr. Olmsted, it's a Prosecution exhibit that had a partial translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And from that same exhibit, the Defence adds the translation of an additional page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Okay. That's sort of how I understood it. But then my question is where is this additional page? Because I don't think I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The additional page is 1D3762. It is translation of that page. And it is on our list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And that's on your list. Okay. Then I think we can move forward. Isn't it, Mr. Olmsted?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I still have not seen the page but at this stage let's go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, can you tell us something about the kind of relations that existed on the one hand between the Ministry of Justice of the RSK and the foreign ministry on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The relations were very decent at first. However, they were disrupted very quickly because we came up with some new demands and new proposals for the way to work. In my first trips to the area of Knin, I had talks with the representatives of the judiciary and I noticed major problems in their operation, and I demanded that they change pronto. The greatest problem was with the operation of the prisons in Glina and in Knin, which held a large number of people without any accompanying documents. Our conclusion was that these people were held there without any investigating judge having made the appropriate ruling to put them in remand, and the police had not completed their pre-investigation work. I sent a letter to the foreign ministry saying that, within three days, we will wait for criminal complaints to see if these people should really be in remand or not. And if we don't receive them, all these people will after three days be released. This caused a great dissatisfaction. The foreign ministry asked us to change the legal provision which stipulated that the maximum detention by the police be extended from three days to 30 days. I did not accept that, and tensions began to rise within the ministry and to shift to the interpersonal level, so the relations between me and Milan Martic became increasingly bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the judiciary, at their meetings or in some other form, point out their problems with the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at least once a week we had meetings of the collegium that included representatives of the judiciary, and we discussed various problems such as lack of personnel and resources. But they also pointed out very sloppily drafted criminal complaints that gave no proper basis for work, and I asked that this be changed in the period that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at 1D2595. That's tab 642.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm checking right now to see whether this is one that's been admitted onto their 65 ter exhibit list. Perhaps Defence counsel can help me out. Is this one of the ones that you raised at the beginning of this witness's testimony, or is this one that there is still a pending motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Zivanovic. Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, does that mean you're admitting it onto their 65 ter list, or should he proceed to a different document or subject matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I didn't admit anything. Mr. Zivanovic asked to have it on the screen, but that's not an admission to the 65 ter list yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's my understanding for the procedure for direct examination that before a document can be used with a witness, it should be on their 65 ter exhibit list. That was the practice we followed in the Prosecution's case in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot say -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So are the parties expecting us to find out whether it's on the list or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am just informed that this document is on our third amended Rule 65 ter list, and I didn't ask the Chamber to admit it on the list but now I would ask if it is possible. It is the subject of the third motion for amended our Rule 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Which we didn't deal with yet, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the 65 ter number, Mr. Zivanovic? There seems to be a little problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is 1D2595.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 2595, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So now you are asking to admit it to your exhibit list, Mr. -- to your 65 ter list, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And what is the Prosecution's position now?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The Prosecution's position is as stated in its response to that motion, which is that it opposed its admission because the Defence have failed to show any due diligence with regard to this document. We have already dealt with one such document. And the same reasoning on the Prosecution part applies, which is this witness was known to the Defence for a long time, this document is not shown to be something that was only recently discovered by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We are losing a lot of time with this, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll not show this document to the evidence, but I stay behind our motion to -- that this document should be admitted into -- should be admitted on our Rule 65 ter list as said in our motion and in our reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, if you don't use it with this witness, that takes the urgency away and we can await the decision on your third motion, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would prefer if it could be decided now because this document is relevant for this witness and we indicated in our Rule 65 ter motion on our list that it is -- it had to be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, but now you say you will not use it. Or am I wrong? You say you will not use it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My intention was to use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And I would use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The problem is, A, we are losing time; and B, you asked to admit it here and now but we don't have the arguments from both sides, the arguments being in the motion and in the response.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From our side, I just would add that this particular document is relevant because it indicates about the matter that the witness mentioned right now about the relationship between the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of the Interior of RSK, and this document clearly indicates the nature of their problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zivanovic, for the moment we will not admit the decision to your 65 ter list, but this decision is without prejudice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Susa, we are going to move to a different subject. You were talking about your opposition to the setting up of military courts in the Republic of the Serbian Krajina. Do you remember if you talked about this publicly in the media?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked about this at government meetings in direct communication with the defence ministry and Ministry of the Interior as well as in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at document 1513 from the Prosecution's list. It's tab 582.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a text that appeared in the press. We can see that the date is the 24th of February.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only see the text in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in English. That is correct. It does not only refer to you and the question of military courts. I am going to read a short part of it that links back to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 2 of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will read it in English and then you will get a translation. It's the first paragraph here that we see. [In English] "And just when it was expected that this would reap results and prevent further robberies, Minister of Justice Vojin Susa wrote a letter in which he accused the army of creating a 'parallel military legal system' that was in contradiction with the regulations of the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Goran Hadzic, which say that in conditions of a state of war, all military legal matters are to be dealt with by civil courts. This was justified by the fact that the military legal system is not regulated by appropriate laws." [Interpretation] Do you remember giving a statement like this to the media?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember giving it, because the background data is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1513 will be Exhibit D229.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, while you were the justice minister and generally, did you command any military or police unit or generally any other armed formation?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were not my competencies and I did not have any desire to do anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a document of the same date as this statement that I have just shown you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is tab 668. The document is from the Prosecutor's list, the 65 ter list. It's document 6540.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is -- I don't even know what this is. Is it a report or something similar, sent by the commander of the Slavonia Baranja Corps, Colonel Sladojevic? I don't see to whom the document was sent. Could you please look at what is said in the first paragraph of the document; namely, that the Red Berets, currently the special unit, I don't know what A/A means, that was established by order of the president of the republic, Goran Hadzic, is currently in Ilok and under the command of the minister of justice. Could you please tell us if you were aware that Goran Hadzic had formed a special unit, either by the name of Red Berets or some other name, that is being referred to here in this document?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware that he formed any kind of unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you did not command any units. Are you able to explain, do you know how you're -- you're referred to here, not by name but by your function, as being in command of a unit?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think 100 per cent here they mean me, and the continuation of this information could have been found in the daily Politika signed by General Mileta Novakovic where all of this is thoroughly dealt with and it's even said which day I did a review of the unit. So the resolution of this situation was quite unexpected because at the time when I was allegedly reviewing the unit, I had already been in Benkovac for two days. Something that Mr. Zecevic, the prime minister, and three other ministers were aware of. Those three or four ministers were actually with me at the time at the hotel in Benkovac. I stated all of this before the government and then it became clear that all of this was a provocation directed primarily at Goran Hadzic. And the following day, a denial was published in the Politika daily where General Novakovic admitted that he had received inaccurate information from the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know how this misinformation came about, about Goran Hadzic forming this unit and you being in command of that unit and that you had reviewed the unit?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Sladojevic really wanted to find out what sort of a unit it was. I mean, he could have asked me. I knew. In the Pajzos zone, which is in the immediate vicinity of Ilok, as early as 1991 there was a Red Beret unit stationed there had which had been founded by the state security of Serbia. This was a unit that had top equipment in order to be able to survey the terrain in depth. They did not carry out any military activities. They were concealed there. And at the same time, they were guarding a capital facility from the time of President Tito. This was a hunting villa or lodge. This is where they were staying and they were staying there when this article was published. Later, just like all the other units that had come from Serbia, it was withdrawn and it returned to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, please tell us how long you stayed at the post of justice minister in the Republic of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the assembly session in Okucani. That is when I accepted the end of my function with a dose of relief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember who was elected justice -- as justice minister in the government of the Serbian Republic of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. That was my learned colleague, Mr. Radomir Kuzet. He was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we see please 1D3762.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, could we have a date on the record for that assembly session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the date or approximate date when this assembly session was held?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was held sometime around the 20th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since we have this whole document on our list, I will show to the witness the first page just for the date, to clarify the date of this session. It is tab 572, Exhibit 1597 from the Prosecution list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that it was this date. It was the first and last assembly meeting that was held in Okucani in any case. There were no others before it or after.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the date, then, for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 20th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And may we see 1D3762.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to show you an excerpt from the record of the meeting that is translated. This is the address by Djordje Bjegovic. Could you please tell us what post he was given at that assembly?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until then he was a minister in Mr. Zecevic's government, just like myself, and now he became the prime minister designate of the new government. And then after this assembly session, he became the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you see here who was suggested as the minister of justice and administration?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it was Mr. Radomir Kuzet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, thank you very much. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Olmsted, are you ready for cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I do have -- before I begin, I've made copies of the witness's 1998 statement that have the paragraphs numbered, because I might be referring to some of the paragraphs and it will be easier, I think, for us to deal with them in that manner. I have English copies for Your Honours, and I have a B/C/S version for Defence counsel and for the witness. And, Your Honours, there is one more statement. Just for the witness's sake, I'd like to give him a copy of his 2014 statement just in case we need to reference it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters also be provided with a statement that has paragraphs numbered? It would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Would the interpreters be all right with an English version?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Has everything been distributed, Mr. Olmsted?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Since Defence counsel touched on the issue the Red Berets, I'll begin there. You've testified that you were familiar with the unit the Red Berets that was sent to the Ilok area by DB Serbia in 1991. You were also aware, weren't you, that this Red Beret unit, some of its members were committing crimes in Western Srem, in particular against the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about one and the same unit of Red Berets which I touched upon in the examination-in-chief, that unit did not participate in any combat around Ilok at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not talking about combat. I'm talking about crimes. That while they were in the area of Ilok, they were engaged in bad behaviour, and in particular they were threatening the remaining non-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I would need official information to that effect, which I don't have. The judiciary bodies never informed me of any proceedings that may have been instigated against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let's take a look at 65 ter 6692. This is tab 180.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And what you are about to see Mr. Susa is a 27 January 1993 UNPROFOR weekly situation assessment, and if I can draw your attention to -- well, actually, I don't know if we have a B/C/S version of this so I'll have to read it to you. But under item 3, it reports that the Ilok area is under the control of the Red Berets from Bapska and that there are reports about threats towards Croats in that area. Now, being based in Ilok, you were aware of these problems with the Red Berets, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of these problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Let us have on the screen 1D3087. This is tab 272.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: This is a Slavonia Baranja Corps security organ report, dated 2 March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 of the English, page 3 of the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: This document reports that you and the Red Berets conducted a search of the Catholic church in Ilok on the 27th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have page 2 before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And now hopefully you can see it. It reports that the Red Berets in your presence conducted a search of a Catholic church on the 27th of February, 1993, at 3.00 p.m. Now, this is highly specific intelligence information about you and your links to the Red Berets, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my records, that never happened. I never conducted a search of a Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would object because the witness stated that he doesn't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is cross-examination and the Prosecution is using this for impeachment purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of impeachment. I don't understand. It is for impeachment purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's what Mr. Olmsted says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1D3087 will be Exhibit P3272.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could have on the screen -- if we may have on the screen 1D3551. This is tab 282. Oh, and, Your Honours, this is a confidential report. Perhaps we should -- perhaps we should go into closed session -- or private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence counsel showed this witness 65 ter 6540. The Defence did not tender it into evidence. The Prosecution believes it's relevant to this line of questioning, and therefore it seeks to admit that into evidence so that the Trial Chamber can see the complete picture with regard to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 6540 will be Exhibit P3274.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, you testified about your friendship with Mr. Hadzic since high school. Do you still --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, we may have some problems with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true. There was a delay in the interpretation. That was the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Susa. You still consider Mr. Hadzic to be your friend, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hadzic is my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: While Mr. Hadzic was a fugitive from this Tribunal between 2004 and 2011, did you have any communications with him via telephone or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, we didn't speak or see each other for approximately ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And after Mr. Hadzic was arrested in July of 2011, did you have any direct communications with him?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never called me, nor I him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your August 2014 statement indicates nine dates between 25 September 2013 and 1 August 2014 that you were interviewed by Mr. Zivanovic or a member of Mr. Hadzic's Defence team. Prior to September 2013, Mr. Hadzic's Defence team consulted you on matters relevant to this case, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say when that started happening. And, yes, they did contact me. There is nothing in dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you recall what year they first contacted you in? Was it the year that he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think that was the following year.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: So please tell us, their contacts with you in the year of 2012, what were the nature of those contacts?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic asked me whether I would be willing to testify as a Defence witness and I agreed. A few months later we met for the first time, we started talking about the Hadzic case. Mr. Zivanovic asked me about my journey through all that was happening from 1991 to the end of my political engagement. Later on we discussed some specific events that I was either involved in or the documents that Mr. Zivanovic assumed I had been involved in drafting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And these discussions that took place in 2012, did they occur prior to the trial beginning against Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The trial had already started.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: So the trial began in September 2012. So these discussions occurred towards the end of 2012; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. As far as I recall, the witness said that he believes that it was one year after. He didn't fix the year 2012. And I see that the Prosecution always used the year 2012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't see the problem, Mr. Zivanovic. You may continue, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'm just trying to pin-point when these discussion occurred, and you say that they occurred a year after he was arrested, so sometime in 2012. You said it was after the trial began. So would it have been towards the end of 2012 that you had these discussions with Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You insist on dates. However, at the time they didn't matter that much. I wouldn't be able to tell you, but I knew by then that Mr. Zivanovic was Mr. Hadzic's legal representative. I don't know whether talks happened in September or October or when. In any case, Mr. Zivanovic made a record of every such interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: While you were in The Hague preparing for your testimony, how many days did you meet with the Hadzic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you the number of hours: Six or seven hours all together, an hour a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: So you were here for, what, two weeks, and you met for only six hours?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps more. I've been here for a long time and I've seen Mr. Zivanovic almost every day. I believe that he was absent for a while. He attended his mother's funeral [as interpreted] or something. But we were here and we reviewed all the documents that have been presented to me here at trial. I really did not keep a record of the time spent in conversations with the Mr. Zivanovic, but it was not a short time, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That's fine. And we apologise that you've been here for so long. Now, you were interviewed by the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor on 10 January 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could bring up 1D2318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I just noted one error in transcript. It is line 17. It was not -- the witness did not mention "funeral" but "memorial service."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. It's noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could bring up 1D2318. This is tab 261.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, sir, this is your 1998 statement that I'm drawing to your attention. Now, prior to signing this statement it was read to you in the Serbian language by an interpreter; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. I told you that that statement had been read to me in Serbian by Miroslav Vasic in Toma Fila's law firm.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Besides signing each page of the statement, you signed the acknowledgement at the end --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could turn to the second-to-last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: -- confirming that the statement was read over to you in the Serbian language and is true to the best of your knowledge and recollection. Now, as an experienced attorney, you're aware of the significance of signing such an acknowledgement; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no reason to doubt the veracity of what was read to me by Mr. Vasic on the premises of Toma Fila's law firm. He represented the Defence of the accused, after all. I was forced to rely on his knowledge of the whole matter. I signed what was read to me by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we can go to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We see that also present that day when this statement was read back to you was Toma Fila, the attorney for Slavko Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could turn to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I think you've already mentioned Mr. Vasic being present. But also present were Vladimir Petrovic and Sanja Leskovac, and they were all members of the Dokmanovic Defence team, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not disputing that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And both Mr. Fila and Mr. Vasic speak English?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possible. I'm sure about Vasic. I don't know about Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could turn to 1D2319, page 32, which is transcript page 3266. This is tab 262.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, on May 26th, 1998, you testified in the Dokmanovic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I don't think we -- I don't know if we have a B/C/S version of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: But at that trial, you testified that this 1998 statement of yours was read back to you in Serbian and you signed the statement as being true and correct. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: I'm telling you how we arrived at the Serbian version. I never saw it in that form. As for that English version, I signed it because Mr. Vasic said that it was okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could just turn to the next page in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And during cross-examination, the attorney for the Prosecution referred to your 1998 statement on a number of occasions, and the only mistake that you pointed out was with regard to the participation of Veselin Sljivancanin at the Velepromet meeting on the 20th of November, 1991; isn't that correct? You didn't point out any other errors.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously there are some parts of the statement which are of interest only for the Dokmanovic case. I'm afraid that Mr. Vasic focused on that part concerning the conduct and the movements of Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic. I had access only to that part of statement that he read back to me and that was important for him. My whole statement is important, in my view and from my point of view, that is, but I heard only the part of the statement that he read back to me. And now, as you're showing the statement to me in English, I really cannot decipher what's important and what's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You testified that the SBWS judiciary began to function at the beginning of November 1991. In carrying out their functions, the SBWS courts and prosecutors' offices, which I'll refer to as "the judiciary" just for simplicity's sake, applied the laws of the SFRY and the Republic of Serbia until the SBWS or the RSK established its own laws; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And with regard to the SFRY laws, the SBWS courts applied, among others, the SFRY Criminal Code and SFRY Criminal Procedure Code?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They applied SFRY laws for the crimes contained therein. Most of the crimes were described in republican criminal codes and those were separately implemented in Croatia and in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The SFRY Law on the Military Courts is another law that was applied in the SBWS until Mr. Hadzic issued by decree an RSK Law on the Military Courts in February of 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could have P2518 on the screen. This is tab 1. And if we could look at Article 1 of the SFRY Law on Military Courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We see that it limits the criminal jurisdiction of the military courts to criminal offences committed by military personnel and those involving certain criminal offences committed by other persons which relate to national defence and state security.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a problem with interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Susa, did you hear what I said or do I need to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. You don't have to repeat. I heard it. Yes, that's what is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we look at page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, when reading from a document, you should pay particular attention to the speed you're reading it. I think that's the basis of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2. And I'm wondering -- no, we want to have P2518 on the left-hand -- on the right-hand screen the English is -- no, I stand corrected. I apologise. Page 2, if we could look at Article 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: This article defines military personnel as including soldiers on compulsory military service, military school cadets, active junior officer, officer, or noncombat specialist, persons from the reserve force while as conscripts on military duty, or a civilian carrying out specific military duty. Mr. Susa, members of the Territorial Defence do not fall within this definition of military personnel; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are not correct. They definitely fall within two categories: Either persons under number 4 or persons under 5. They're either from the reserve force or civilians performing some military duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, I'll put to you that being a member of a TO unit does not mean that you are a reserve officer. That is -- or reserve -- member of the reserve force. Rather, the TO was separate under the SFRY Law on All People's Defence from the JNA and police. That's in Article 102 of that law.

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that you are not right, because at the moment when front lines are opened and war activities begin, the Territorial Defence begins to function under the command of the army and as an integral part of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That would be the case if they were resubordinated to the army but it's not necessarily the case; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they are resubordinated to the army, that's the way they operate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the witness should see this provision of the law the Prosecution referred to. It is Article 102 of Law on All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Defence counsel can certainly show that to this witness during re-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But it was part of the question of the Prosecution concerning this particular provision, and it would be fair to show that to the witness, this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I agree with Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. Olmsted, unless the witness says that he knows what is in Article 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could have L10 on the screen. This is tab 2. And if we could turn to page 64 of the English, page 17 of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to Article 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And in the English if we could -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: It states: "Territorial Defence shall comprise all armed formations which are not incorporated in the Yugoslav People's Army and the police." And --

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that's the position. It's not written in that article. Maybe there is another article?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May we -- if we could turn the page. Is it -- page of the original version. I think it's in the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And perhaps you see it now. "The Territorial Defence shall comprise all armed formations which are not incorporated in the Yugoslav People's Army and the police." And, sir, that is what we were just talking about. Because all the Territorial Defence is not resubordinated to the army, it was separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, maybe it should be more precise. What Territorial Defence was not resubordinated? What part of Territorial Defence, from which area or from ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't see any problem with the theoretical question as such, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think the Prosecutor is showing me the right article. Article 103 would be much more relevant, which says something slightly different from what the Prosecutor is putting to me. I really had no occasion to familiarise myself properly with this law, but in any case, it's quite obvious what Article 103 says and you can see who, and when, controls the Territorial Defence. This is a bit different from what the Prosecutor was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, as your knowledge of this law is clearly limited, we'll move on. But let me ask you this: Paramilitary groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I think we would like to see at this point in time Article 103. I suppose it's the next page in the English version. There it is. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just turning briefly to paramilitary groups, armed paramilitary groups. They did not fall within the definition of military personnel because by definition they were outside the army; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJIN SUSA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could go back to P2518, the Law on Military Courts. Well, Your Honours, I see the time, and perhaps two minutes is not enough to even go into the next matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Susa, this is it for today. We expect you to be back tomorrow morning at 9.00. And as previously said, you are still a witness under oath. You may not discuss your testimony with anybody and you cannot have contact with any of the parties. Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of October, 2014, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.57 p.m.,
